h: Get the most from your climb
p: First-time climbers often wonder what to expect, so here's the lowdown. You'll be shown how the harness works and how to clip on and off the auto-belays safely, then you're free to explore. Start with the easier walls to get a feel for it, then work your way up to the trickier challenges. There's no pressure to reach the top every time, and letting go to drop back down is all part of the fun.

Clip 'n Climb is a cracking choice for birthday parties, and plenty of families book it for that reason. If you're planning one, booking well ahead helps, especially at weekends and in school holidays. For everyday sessions, arriving a little early means you'll be relaxed and ready when your slot starts. Spectating friends and family can usually watch from the side, so not everyone needs to climb.

Croydon has plenty to round off the day. Fairfield Halls, the big arts venue in the centre, hosts concerts, comedy and family shows. If you fancy fresh air, Lloyd Park and Wandle Park are both handy green spaces, and Addington Hills offers a viewing platform with sweeping views across London on a clear day. History fans can visit the Airport House visitor centre at the former Croydon Airport, which tells the story of London's original international airport and opens on selected days. Getting around is easy too, thanks to the Tramlink network, which links Croydon with Wimbledon, Beckenham and New Addington, and East and West Croydon stations offer frequent trains into central London.
